subject: Urgent: PayFlux reserved throughput gap & GPU pool saturation
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@payflux.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@payflux.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: sustained 5xx and p95 latency spike – reserved pool appears throttled

Sofia,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and p95 latency on our checkout inference calls since ~08:45 UTC. Key indicators:
- p50 ~ 120ms (normal) but p95 up to 2.8s and p99 > 4s.
- 5xx rate has climbed from baseline ~0.2% to ~3.6% in last 20m.
- Our reserved capacity (EU-dedicated pool) is reporting queueing and token rejections (quota exceeded / throttled) for customer_key PF-ENT-09.

This is impacting user checkout flows for ~10% of requests (we surface a retry which is causing double-charges risk). We have an open monitoring dashboard attached that shows the anomaly (payflux_sla_dash.pdf).

We need immediate remediation and executive visibility — this is customer critical and on the renewal cycle. Please confirm what you can route/fallback us to, and whether you can authorize additional burst capacity while you triage root cause.

Can you also confirm where we should send sample request_ids and logs? We can share a set within the next 10 minutes.

Thanks,

Lena Brooks
Head of Platform
PayFlux

Attachment: payflux_sla_dash.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@payflux.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 5xx and p95 latency spike – reserved pool appears throttled

Lena —

Thanks for the heads up and the dashboard. I'm very sorry for the user impact; we recognize how time-sensitive this is.

Immediate actions:
1) I'm standing up an ops bridge now and looped SRE and our Cx lead (Jonas, Marissa, David on cc).
2) Please send a sample of 10 request_ids and timestamps to this thread (or upload to the Drive link below) — we'll prioritize those logs.
3) We've triggered a PagerDuty incident (PF-INC-4621) and will post updates every 30 minutes until resolved.

I'll follow up within 20 minutes with an operational mitigation plan (routing/fallback + burst options).

Again — sincere apologies. We're treating this as P1 and will escalate to execs for burst authorization if needed.

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Urgent: sustained 5xx and p95 latency spike – reserved pool appears throttled

Team — quick technical readout from infra:

Findings (10:00 UTC):
- We observe GPU utilization hitting sustained 98-100% on PayFlux's dedicated pool (eu-west-1-dedicated-42).
- Queue lengths on the inference router for PF-ENT-09 spiked, causing request timeouts and token rejections.
- Root trigger appears to be a model variant rollout at PayFlux (higher context usage + KV-cache misses) producing larger memory footprint per session; this multiplied by a small batch-window shift increased per-token work.

Immediate mitigations we can execute within 15m:
A) Route PayFlux traffic to a fallback variant: gpt-open-quant-8 (compatible latency profile, slightly lower throughput but avoids the kernel path causing memory blowout). This is a config change we can apply to their routing policy immediately and revert once fixed.
B) Purge prefix/KV cache for PF-ENT-09 to free memory pressure (will cause short-term cold-start cost but reduces queueing).
C) Request temporary burst: +20% dedicated capacity for EU pool (requires ops lead + Marissa sign-off for financial/exec authorization). If approved, we can spin up nodes in ~12-18 minutes.
D) Apply conservative per-request token limits for PayFlux while we triage (500 token cap) to prevent runaway sessions.

Attachments: pod_metrics_agg.csv (aggregated GPU/pod metrics for the last 90 minutes).

Ask: Marissa — can you approve a one-time burst authorization and short credit against PF-2026-ENT-09? If we can't get burst approved in <30m, we'll need to implement A + D as immediate protective controls and prioritize a hotfix.

I'll be on the bridge (PD incident) and will post updates.

Jonas Weber
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@payflux.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Summary & next steps — PayFlux incident (PF-INC-4621)

Lena —

Thanks for your patience this morning. Quick summary of what we executed and the plan moving forward:

What we did (complete):
- Temporarily routed PayFlux to fallback model variant gpt-open-quant-8 at 09:50 UTC. This immediately reduced GPU pressure and dropped 5xx rate from ~3.6% to ~0.4% within 9 minutes.
- Purged PayFlux prefix/KV cache at 09:52 UTC; cold starts contributed ~0.6s on a minority of requests but prevented queueing cascades.
- Applied a conservative request token cap (500 tokens) for PayFlux at 10:05 UTC while we validate model footprint.

Pending (next 48 hours):
- Jonas is leading an RCA to identify why the model variant induced cache thrash and to produce a mitigation patch (kernel scheduling + memory guards). Target: initial RCA draft by 2027-05-26 18:00 UTC.
- We requested a one-time +20% burst allocation; Marissa (cc) is authorizing a temporary credit now. If approved, we will scale additional nodes and backfill capacity; ETA for nodes: ~15 minutes from approval.
- We'll coordinate a rollout checklist with PayFlux for any future model variant changes (preflight traffic shaping, resource impact tests).

Customer-facing note: we will not change PayFlux's SLA status for this incident; we propose a goodwill credit (2% of May invoice) pending Marissa's sign-off.

If PayFlux can share the model variant hash and the exact rollout time, that will accelerate the RCA. Lena — can you drop those artifacts to the Drive link and confirm a convenient time for a short wrap-up call?

PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PF-INC-4621
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/PayFlux/investigation-20270525

I'll keep you posted on the RCA progress and will update this thread as we have a remediation plan.

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
